items.evidence: 26.1.1's jar HAS DirtPathBlock (no PathBlock); the export chain is ['DirtPathBlock','Block']. But the 26.1.1 tree's classes.rs:208 (byte-identical to 26.1's) reads Path = "PathBlock" only — the "DirtPathBlock" alias 26.2's tree carries was dropped. The class resolves to plain Block, so every path arm is dead: survive (survive.rs:273), updateShape, scheduled tick (tick.rs:202, unconditional turn_to_base_block), placement. Dirt paths never revert to dirt when the block above becomes solid, and never revert on schedule. Vanilla 26.1.1 DirtPathBlock is byte-identical to 26.1's. Fix note: add "DirtPathBlock" to the Path alias (the 26.2 form), with the unit test 26.2's tree carries.
items.title: Dirt path never reverts: DirtPathBlock unmapped in classes.rs (REPRODUCES from 26.1)

items.evidence: Two independent causes, either alone sufficient. (a) Class dispatch dead: 26.1.1 has no SpeleothemBlock (PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly, javap-verified; export chain ['PointedDripstoneBlock','Block']), so the Class::Speleothem arms never fire: scheduled tick to spawn_falling_stalactite (tick.rs:248), random tick to growth (tick.rs:434), survive (survive.rs:307), updateShape (shapes.rs:728), placement (place.rs:1156). (b) Tag predicates dead: #speleothems is ABSENT from 26.1.1 data (block-tags.json and the client jar), so speleothem.rs:15, falling.rs:55, place.rs:1407, shapes.rs:1189 all fail; vanilla 26.1.1 uses hardcoded Blocks.POINTED_DRIPSTONE checks instead. Observable: dripstone never grows, stalactites never fall, can_survive defaults true (floating dripstone never pops), placement tip direction/thickness never computed. Fix note: dispatch on PointedDripstoneBlock directly and replace the #speleothems tag reads with a hardcoded pointed-dripstone check, matching vanilla 26.1.1's own form. While fixing, also fix the latent B5-G16: vanilla canGrow requires the fluid two blocks above to be WATER and a source (isSource()); the port (speleothem.rs:104-107) checks only FluidKind::Water. Unobservable while growth is dead, so not minted separately.
items.title: Dripstone fully dead: no SpeleothemBlock class in 26.1.1 AND #speleothems tag absent (REPRODUCES from 26.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 HAS bonemeal height gates (unlike 1.21.7), re-verified fresh by javap: SaplingBlock.isValidBonemealTarget = ServerLevel AND isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(getMinimumHeight)); AzaleaBlock = same + 2 and fluid above empty; MushroomBlock = feature exists AND AbstractHugeMushroomFeature AND HugeMushroomFeatureConfiguration AND isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(4 + foliageRadius)). The port's bonemeal_valid (bonemeal.rs:326-360) matches in form, but tree_minimum_height (growth.rs:446-453) reads json["trunk_placer"]["base_height"] at the JSON top level, while the stored feature JSON nests it under config — configured_json (worldgen/live.rs:234) returns the raw whole feature JSON. So it always returns 0 (vanilla base heights: oak 4, spruce 5, mangrove 2, azalea 4, birch 5, jungle 4, acacia 5, cherry 7, dark/pale oak 6). Same nesting bug for mushrooms: the port reads json["foliage_radius"] top-level (bonemeal.rs:353) but it lives under config (brown = 3, red = 2); the port always uses 2 — red correct by luck, brown's gate is pos.y+6 instead of pos.y+7. isBonemealSuccess (sapling/azalea 0.45, mushroom/fungus 0.4) matches vanilla exactly. Fix note: read config.trunk_placer.base_height and config.foliage_radius (or make configured_json return the config object). The opposite direction (too strict) is the NEW item B5-G29 — both directions are live at once in 26.1.1.
items.title: Bonemeal validity too permissive at the build ceiling: sapling/azalea/mushroom height gates read the wrong JSON level (REPRODUCES from 26.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 ChorusFlowerBlock.randomTick proceeds when above.y <= getMaxY() (320) — bytecode if_icmple 28, re-verified fresh. The port (tick.rs:1430, chorus_flower_random_tick, file byte-identical to 26.1's) returns early when above_pos.y > max_y() - 1, i.e. above.y >= 320. A flower at pos.y == 319: vanilla still ages/branches (horizontal targets at y=319 are in-bounds); the port returns early and the flower stays forever young. The rest of the chorus logic matches exactly (age < 5, support/pillar logic, height < 2 || height <= rand(5 or 4), grow-up with allNeighborsEmpty + empty at +2, branch attempts rand(4) + pillar?1:0, events 1033/1034, age-5 death).
items.title: Chorus flower never ticks at the build ceiling (REPRODUCES from 26.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 BellBlock.isProperHit (bytecode read fresh in full) requires click_y > 0.8123999834060669 — hit the UPPER part of the bell — plus a non-Y face plus attachment/axis rules (floor: facing axis == hit axis; single/double wall: axes differ; ceiling: always). The port (redstone.rs:1442, bell_hit; the redstone.rs tree diff touches only the diode guard, B2-G07) requires click_y <= 0.8124f32 — inverted. Hits at the top ring ring in vanilla but not in the port; hits at the bottom ring ring in the port but not in vanilla. The attachment/axis arms match; bell_ring (block event 1 + sound volume 2.0 pitch 1.0 + BLOCK_CHANGE) matches vanilla attemptToRing.
items.title: Bell isProperHit height comparison inverted (REPRODUCES from 26.1)

items.evidence: The port reads #convertible_to_mud (with 'i') in four places: data.rs:460 (tag table), horizon-client/src/game/potions.rs:710 (water bottle use), horizon-client/src/game/remote.rs:8658, horizon-client/src/game/dispenser.rs:2245 (dispenser water bottle). 26.1.1's tag is #convertable_to_mud (with 'a') — verified three ways: BlockTags.CONVERTABLE_TO_MUD in the jar, data/minecraft/tags/block/convertable_to_mud.json in the client jar (dirt, coarse_dirt, rooted_dirt), and vanilla PotionItem.useOn checks it (bytecode offset 57, re-verified fresh). items.title: Water bottle on dirt never makes mud: port reads #convertible_to_mud, 26.1.1's tag is #convertable_to_mud (REPRODUCES from 26.1)

items.evidence: The port's portal_frame() (portal.rs:40-44, file byte-identical to 26.1's) reads #nether_portal_frame, which is ABSENT from 26.1.1 data (verified in block-tags.json; no synthesis anywhere in the tree) — always false. items.evidence: The port's motion_blocking_top (weather.rs:41-59, file byte-identical to 26.1's) reads #blocks_motion_in_heightmap, which is ABSENT from 26.1.1 data (verified in block-tags.json; no synthesis anywhere in the tree) — only fluids count as motion-blocking. Vanilla 26.1.1 Heightmap.MATERIAL_MOTION_BLOCKING is a method reference to BlockStateBase.blocksMotion() (bootstrap method 1 in Heightmap, re-verified fresh with javap -v). Consequence: precipitation_info computes top = min_y in fluidless columns — snow never accumulates on land and ice never forms except on water. The same wrong top also feeds is_raining_at (weather.rs:127), lightning strike height (lightning.rs:199), and portal-travel spawn height (portal_travel.rs:506). 26.2's tree correctly used per-state blocksMotion(). NEW site in 26.1.1 (same root cause): feature_world.rs:350-360 also regressed — the 26.1 tree's blocks_motion() reads there were replaced with #blocks_motion_in_heightmap / #blocks_motion_in_heightmap_no_leaves tag reads (both tags absent), so feature-placement heightmaps (OceanFloor, MotionBlocking, MotionBlockingNoLeaves) are broken the same way; recorded here as an additional site of this item. Fix note: replace the tag reads with the per-state blocksMotion() value from the prepared data (26.2's form), or synthesise the tag at prepare time from it.
items.title: Snow never accumulates on land, ice never forms except on water: motion_blocking_top reads the absent #blocks_motion_in_heightmap tag (REPRODUCES from 26.1; extended)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 ComposterBlock composts by a static chance table: COMPOSTABLES (Object2FloatMap<ItemLike>, 115 entries) and addItem (bytecode read fresh): level 0 + chance > 0 adds a layer with NO roll; above level 0 it adds one when the level random rolls under the chance (nextDouble() < chance). The 26.1 tree implemented exactly this (compost_chance, 115/115 exact). The 26.1.1 tree replaced it with the 26.3 form: horizon-items/src/items.rs:1015 populates the item's compostable field ONLY from the minecraft:compostable component — and ZERO of the 1,506 items in the prepared 26.1.1 items.json carry that component (26.1.1 vanilla has no compostable component; 26.3 added it). compost_chance does not exist anywhere in the 26.1.1 tree (grep: zero hits). game/composter.rs:29-38 therefore returns None for every item: use_composter returns false (no hand composting), composter_container_insert returns the stack untouched (no hopper composting), villager_insert_item returns early (no villager composting), composter_takes is false for every held item. The level side (level/interact.rs:559-633) lost composter_add_item entirely: composter_insert/composter_layer now take a layers count directly, so the level-0-always-adds rule and the chance roll exist nowhere in the tree. Observable: no item can ever be composted in the 26.1.1 port by any path. (The level-7 to 8 tick itself still functions if a composter reaches level 7 by command; the insertion path is what is dead.) Fix note: restore the 26.1 form — the compost_chance table plus composter_add_item with the level-0 rule.
items.title: Composter completely dead: the port reads the minecraft:compostable component no 26.1.1 item carries (NEW)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 BedBlock.useWithoutItem (bytecode read fresh): client returns SUCCESS_SERVER; if part != HEAD, redirect to the head and require only that the head is this bed (else CONSUME); a HEAD click needs no foot check at all — it proceeds straight to the BED_RULE path (sleep or explode). The 26.1 tree matched this. The 26.1.1 tree's Class::AbstractBed arm (interact.rs:367-384) implements the 26.3 pair check: it requires the block at the other half's position to be this bed with the opposite part, else returns Consume. Note: the 26.1.1 tree's sleep_height change in game/beds.rs (shape-top form) is NOT a defect — for every 26.1.1 bed the shape top is 9/16 = 0.5625 and pos_to_bed adds 0.125, giving exactly vanilla's flat 0.6875 (LivingEntity.setPosToBed, javap-verified); the straw-bed branch is dead (no straw_bed in the 26.1.1 export).
items.title: Bed use requires the other half: a head click with no foot returns Consume instead of sleeping (NEW)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 SaplingBlock.isValidBonemealTarget is ONLY the height check (ServerLevel AND isInsideBuildHeight(pos.above(getMinimumHeight)), javap-verified fresh) — there is no canGrow method on 26.1.1's TreeGrower at all. The 26.1 tree matched this, with a comment noting canGrow (the 2x2 requirement for a mega-only grower) is 26.3-only, so a lone dark oak sapling takes the meal (and consumes it 45% of the time with no growth). The 26.1.1 tree's bonemeal_valid (bonemeal.rs:335) adds !self.tree_can_grow(g, pos, state) — tree_can_grow (growth.rs:425-444) returns false for a mega-only grower (dark oak, pale oak — empty trees list, non-empty mega_trees) with no 2x2 square. The gate also draws random (weighted on both lists) on EVERY sapling/azalea validity check, shifting the RNG stream where vanilla draws nothing. The 26.1.1 tree's own growth_tests.rs now asserts the refusal (lone_dark_oak_sapling_cannot_grow) where the 26.1 test asserted the meal is taken. items.title: Bonemeal validity too strict: the 26.3 canGrow gate refuses lone dark/pale oak saplings (NEW — 1.21.7 G15's original form returns)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 TreeGrower (bytecode + fields read fresh) is the secondary-chance form: 10 growers (oak, spruce, mangrove, azalea, birch, jungle, acacia, cherry, dark oak, pale oak — NO poplar), secondaryChance float, megaTree/secondaryMegaTree/tree/secondaryTree/flowers/secondaryFlowers optionals. getConfiguredFeature draws ONE nextFloat() unconditionally (even at chance 0) against secondaryChance; getConfiguredMegaFeature draws only when a secondary mega tree exists (spruce only). The 26.1 tree implemented exactly this (with three unit tests pinning the draw counts). The 26.1.1 tree replaced it with the 26.3 weighted-list form (growth.rs:145-269): trees/mega_trees/flower_trees weight lists plus weighted() (growth.rs:249-264, next_int_bound(total)), a shortest field, and a poplar grower (dead — no poplar_sapling in the 26.1.1 export). Observable: the probabilities coincide (oak fancy 10%, mangrove tall 85%, spruce mega 50/50) but the draw type (nextInt vs nextFloat) and draw count differ — jungle's mega draw happens in the port (total 1) where vanilla draws nothing, and every single-tree grower draws nextInt(1) where vanilla draws a float — so the chosen tree (fancy vs regular oak, tall vs short mangrove, mega spruce vs mega pine) and the RNG stream after it diverge from vanilla for the same seed. Fix note: restore the 26.1 secondary-chance form and its tests.
items.title: TreeGrower rewritten in the 26.3 weighted-list form: tree selection diverges from vanilla's secondary-chance draws (NEW)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.1 TreeGrower.growTree, mega path (bytecode read fresh, offsets 90-288): clears the 2x2 square to Blocks.AIR with flags 260 and restores the PASSED sapling state on failure, also with flags 260. The 26.1 tree matched this. The 26.1.1 tree's grow_tree (growth.rs:384-419) removes each sapling via remove_sapling (growth.rs:375-382) — the fluid's legacy block with flags 818 (UPDATE_SKIP_ALL_SIDEEFFECTS | UPDATE_CLIENTS) — and restores the collected per-position states on failure. Note UPDATE_NONE IS 260 in the port's flag table, mod.rs:164.) Fix note: restore the 26.1 mega path (air + flags 260, restore the passed state) and the single-path flags.
items.title: Mega sapling growth leaves water where vanilla 26.1.1 leaves air (NEW — 1.21.7 G14's form returns for the mega path)

systemic_note: The 26.1.1 tree is a stale re-port from 26.2/26.3 form, not a carry-forward of the 26.1 tree (Batch 2's §6 finding, confirmed in B5 scope): every 26.1 defect reproduces AND the tree adds fourteen NEW behaviour defects and one NEW oracle defect, each a one-method reversion to the 26.2/26.3 form the 26.1 tree deliberately removed — ice melt (G23), ice mining (G24), tripwire (G25), eyeblossom (G26), beds (G27), dragon eggs (G28), bonemeal gates (G29/G30/G31/G32), TreeGrower (G33/G34), digging events (G35), composter (G22), ReplaceBlock oracle (O04). The 26.1 tree is the repair reference for all fifteen: each fix note says 'restore the 26.1 form', and the 26.1 tree's own comments name each distinction. The absent-tag root cause got WORSE: the 26.1.1 tree reads MORE absent tags than the 26.1 tree did (#blocks_motion, #blocks_motion_in_heightmap[_no_leaves] in feature_world, #blocks_fluid_flow, #sculk_growth_inhibitors in level/sculk.rs) — and the tag table resolves absent tags to EMPTY sets (data.rs:396 .unwrap_or_default()) while tag() returns Option (mod.rs:941-942), so every absent-tag read silently degrades to false, never an error. The composter (G22) is the only whole-block regression: no item can be composted by any path, because the port reads the 26.3 minecraft:compostable component no 26.1.1 item carries (0/1,506 items).
